materials.label: Hittite selective adaptation through trained scribal practice
materials.what_audience_follows: The Hittite case lets the audience follow cuneiform arriving through external specialist traditions, being learned and modified for a new linguistic environment, while only selected Mesopotamian practices travel with it.
sequence: Cuneiform reaches Anatolian courts and specialists through contact with established scribal traditions.
Training uses lexical and bilingual material to reproduce competence across a new community of practice.
Scribes adapt sign values and orthographic conventions rather than simply substituting Hittite words into an unchanged system.
The receiving tradition adopts selected scholarly and literary practices while other Mesopotamian administrative conventions do not transfer uniformly.

locators: pp. 3–13: Hittite curricula, bilingual lists and selective transfer on the cuneiform periphery

limitations: This is a process carrier synthesized from a bounded scholarly discussion, not a single excavated event sequence.
The Hittite case cannot stand for every region that adopted cuneiform.
Do not imply that all Mesopotamian bookkeeping/metrology disappeared from Anatolia; the claim is selective and non-uniform transfer.

gaps: If the outline wants a scene-level Hittite adoption episode, WS07 still needs an object-level source locator; the present material is strong enough for a process carrier but not for invented dialogue or a single adoption moment.
